newsitem.title: VIETNAM: UNICEF says child exploitation growing in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: UNICEF says child exploitation growing in Vietnam.

text.p: A United Nations official in Hanoi warned on Monday that child exploitation was increasing in Vietnam and reported evidence that some children were having to work long hours in dangerous conditions for no pay.
Rima Salah of the U.N. Children's Fund (UNICEF) said in a statement that Vietnam's opening to the market economy had brought the issue of child labour to the fore.
The statement said there was evidence that children below the age of 16 were facing increased risks of economic exploitation.

"There is evidence of children exploited in gold mines, children working as domestic servants at a very young age or children working up to 14 hours a day in hazardous conditions for a meagre salary or no payment," Salah said.

Children in Vietnam, one of the world's poorest countries, often help their parents by working at home or in the fields. Accurate assessment of the extent of exploitation can therefore be difficult to gauge.
The government estimates that around 29,000 children below the age of 15 are victims of exploitative labour.
But Salah said the figures were deceptive as most children working in Vietnam were doing so in the informal sector, away from official attention.
"Therefore, the number of children working for long hours in conditions hazardous to their health and mental development is probably higher than estimates reveal," the statement said.
